content: Do not take more or less of this medication than prescribed, and do not stop taking it (or any other HIV medications) without your doctor’s explicit instructions, even for a short period of time. Common side effects may include headache, nausea, vomiting, difficulty sleeping, or loss of appetite. These effects are generally mild, but if they persist or worsen, consult your healthcare provider. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to your health outweigh the potential risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to combat infections that were already present in your body, potentially causing symptoms of those diseases to reappear. Additionally, an overactive immune response may occur, leading to symptoms. This reaction can happen at any time, whether shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. While taking this medication, you may experience a loss of body fat in areas such as the face, arms, legs, and buttocks. This effect may be permanent. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or difficulty breathing, seek immediate medical attention. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Before taking zidovudine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. If you are using the liquid form of this medication, be aware that it may contain sugar. Exercise caution if you have diabetes or any condition requiring you to limit sugar intake. If you are pregnant, inform your doctor before using this medication. Treatment with zidovudine can reduce the risk of transmitting HIV to your baby. However, this medication does pass into breast milk, so discuss breastfeeding with your doctor. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Other medications may affect the removal of zidovudine from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Do not take this medication with other drugs containing zidovudine. Always check the labels of your other prescription medications to ensure they do not contain zidovudine. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While taking this medication, regular lab and medical tests (such as blood counts, liver function tests, viral load, and T-cell counts) should be performed to monitor your progress and detect any potential side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
